correctness.rationale: For any nontrivial Steiner triple system, its complementary three-element base family has size \(v(v-1)(v-3)/6\), point degree \((v-1)(v-3)/2\), and pair codegree \(v-3\). The exact point/pair-incidence character expansion proves the residue four modulo eight at orders congruent to five or seven modulo eight, and the residue zero modulo eight at orders congruent to one or three modulo eight. In the first two classes every integer multiplier is nonzero with two-adic valuation two. Orthogonal Walsh diagonalization yields full rank, the Hilbert-space inverse bound and \(\nu_2(\det T)=2^{v+1}\). The checker independently verifies 74368 exact coefficients in five explicit systems (128, 512, 8192, 32768, and 32768) and tests two nonisomorphic order-15 distributions; infinite proof does not depend on enumerations.

value.rationale: This exact global nonvanishing result is a natural Fourier-convolution invariant for rank-three Steiner matroid bases, applying to every system at infinitely many admissible orders even though the input family is even-sized. Exact determinant valuations give an integral arithmetic consequence. At order 15 two nonisomorphic systems have different full multiplier distributions yet the same universal nonvanishing law, while the adjacent order 9 is singular at any two-point frequency. The question is therefore design-independent structural Fourier stability, not a trivial enumerative restatement.
